Living in a fast-paced World, we have forgotten about the night trains. Especially that they used to be a privilege and not a torture. It is time to slow down and rewind. This project pushes the common boundaries and explores the way in which a re-invented sleeper train concept can improve our life. Although already gaining demand, in order to compete with other contemporary ways of transportation, trains should offer a new and appealing experience in return.

The metallic structures are the support to create types of seating and public furniture but also to illuminate and activate these plots during the night. The center of Chile’s capital receives a daily floating population of 1.8 million people. The city has undergone changes due to gentrification and densification among others issues, which has resulted in a lack of public spaces. An old building is falling appart. They want to destroy the Rothornhütte. This projet strives to preserve the refuge with the help of the hikers. Each one of us will carry some wood up there in order to build lateral reinforced structures. The intervention aims to inhabit these new spaces by using them as place of bivouac, restaurant or toilets. The extensions allow a modern use of the hut in winter as in summer.

proj.t: Dance Trigger. An Infrustructure for Collective Dance
proj.d: Eluding finite labels, Dance Trigger is something in-between a character, totem and machine. Observing her surrounding, she stands and patiently waits for passersby to break from their daily hustle. When noticed, in return she plays her favourite tracks, trying to create an opportunity for collective dancing. She believes that universal language of moving, equally shared by all creatures, can foster a weakening feeling of togetherness. She simply wants to know ‘When was the last time you danced?

proj.t: 13 characters in search of a story
proj.d: The starting point of this project is a theoretical work about the Festival du film fantastique d’Avoriaz, a festival of horror and fantastic cinema that took place between 1973 and 1993 in the french alps. The ritual of a film festival is decomposed and all the functions are spread into small structures. Thirteen constructions inspired by tropes of horror and fantastic cinema are built, each of them portraying one archetype character. The goal is to reflect on the universal value of such tropes and to express their meaning beyond the closed boundaries of a one-hour-and-a-half movie. proj.t: HERBARIUM OF INTERIORS: A Milk Bar, Curaté par India Mahdavi
proj.d: Alcova, Salon du meuble, Milan Un herbier est un spécimen qui devient sa propre image. À mi-chemin entre l’image, la maquette 1:1 et l’objet, l’herbier est multi-format. De la même façon, les intérieurs contemporains empruntent des directions multiples, de l’objet à l’image, des médias à l’espace. Bien qu’ils existent dans des supports et des formats divers, les espaces deviennent physiques dans des instances et des itérations variées. Les intérieurs contemporains sont-ils comme des herbiers, des espaces dont l’image oscille entre la fiction et sa représentation ? Nina F. D’Elia H. (1989) is a Mexican-Italian interior architect and designer based in Geneva, Switzerland. Her work explores the contemporary role that interior architecture plays in global issues, such as the production of physical spaces that cater an ever growing and unregulated digital world and the implications of interior architecture in relation to climate injustices and inequalities. Through her MAIA final diploma project TRASHMANSHIP, Nina investigates the use of waste as an alternative raw material in order to replace the exploitation of finite natural resources, using analog techniques and digital technologies. The project explores the meaning of the truffle in the brand of the Barcelona-based chocolatier Sita Brown. Through an experimental laboratory, which unfolds in different urban scenarios by means of < happenings >, the meticulous process of creating her truffle is shown in slow motion, from the least common multiple that connects her truffle with the landscape to the final delicacy and crafted product. Sen’i Collection consists of selected pieces of furniture imagined specifically for the vestibule, the area by which you enter a building or a house. The space serves as a passageway making a transition between the outside and the inside. All too often neglected, compared to the other rooms in the house, the vestibule, however, communicates to the visitor the first impressions and atmospheres of the interior. The project was inspired by the Genkan, the traditional Japanese entryway for a house, appartement, or building. Les salles de projection se sont peu à peu définies comme des interfaces sociales. La particularité du rituel du cinéma consiste à rassembler dans un espace clos et pour un instant relativement court, des personnes d’identités différentes. De plus, l’instant vécu ne s’appréhende pas uniquement par le ressenti physique ou tactile. Une expérience particulière d’une dimension multisensorielle est perçue par le corps tout entier. Cette réflexion tente de mettre en lumière la relation inconsciente présente entre le corps et l’espace. "Not obsolete anymore!" explore les objets désuets du 18ème au 19ème siècle. Les objets sont des témoins précieux de leur temps et des usages d’une certaine époque. Il n’y a pas si longtemps, la fabrication d’objets relevait plus de l’art que de l’industrie. Depuis, les techniques de fabrication et les matériaux ont radicalement changé par rapport aux siècles précédents. Suivant l’évolution, certains objets sont devenus obsolètes, voire ont disparu. Le projet souhaite faire un pas en arrière, et questionner notre rapport aux objets, mais aussi à notre façon de concevoir. KITA ,is envisioned as a children day care center, in which old building components find a new spatial dimension, responding to the contemporary necessity of climatic issue. It investigates the changing patterns of migration between the city and the villages and their potential to become a new social institution. The project seeks to re-use materials from the abandoned rural landscape, reflecting upon the existing material resources, the embedded heritage of the previous uses and its economic circulation through architecture and sustainability. «Il convivio» «Il convivio» a scenography that investigates the theme of staging rituals as a simulacrum of heritage. The installation is created with the aim of staging the symbolic nature of the celebrative meal. This enactment becomes the physical translation of the intimacy that is created when we share a meal. The structure and objects are designed with different techniques, to enable a total engagement of the senses. Contemporary industrial processes, are used in parallel with ancestral handmade techniques, to emphasize the power of combining different forms of creation. proj.t: CIRCA DIEM: Seoul Biennale of Architecture and Urbanism 2021
proj.d: The CIRCA DIEM project is developed by EPFL and HEAD – Genève for the Seoul Biennale of Architecture and Urbanism 2021. The installation raises awareness about the impact of our daily exposure to light and its dynamics in dense urban environments, which becomes even more important when considering underground life. Circa diem – “about one day” in Latin – is at the origin of what we call our “circadian rhythms” and suggests here a deep and essential link with the natural day-night cycle. Light regulates our neurophysiology according to the natural day-night cycle and thus profoundly affects the liveability of dense cities, in which we tend to live increasingly indoors and deeper underground.

For the SCENES DE NUIT research programme, MA students of MAIA at HEAD – Genève are invited to explore the obscure, underwater depths through the conception and realisation of still lifes with the constraint of using essentially food elements and light. Plunged into darkness, the three-dimensional paintings become supports for photography and filming in order to offer another view of the night on different scales. The results will be exhibited during a large exploratory dinner organised by HiFLOW and designer Eleonore Grignon. The question of transparency is central to contemporary societies. Phenomena of ecological and social impacts only reach arenas of public debate when they are ‘rendered visible’ in terms of data, tracking and information. Whereas modern architecture built its discourse upon the paradigm of visual or phenomenal transparency, contemporary interior architecture envisions the discipline as a web of social, material and media associations. PRODUCTION LINE explores how individual buildings are part of this larger web, and how interior architecture operates at the intersection of physical and social constructs. Updated as a magnificent Herbarium of Interiors in Milan, these spaces replicate not their original images but their mythologies, experiences, and associated cultures. Workshop Inaugural Week – Villa Romaine Toulon, September 2019 Roman villa in Hyère, France Workshop HEAD-Geneva and Camondo School, Toulon. Students were ask to build temporary structures within the Roman Villa in Hyères, a former neoclassical residence from 1880 and currently classified as a historical heritage. Retracing the history of the villa, the installations responded to the site’s unique atmosphere, blurring the boundaries between domestic space and public space, between exterior and interior, between the past and the present. WHAT'S THE FUTURE OF HUMANITARIAN DESIGN? Join us for the presentation of "The Future of Humanitarian Design" (HUD), a four-year research project funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF) . HUD explores how architecture, technology, and political science can address the increasing challenges in humanitarian action. As humanitarian crises worsen, HUD combines diverse disciplines to co-design sociopolitical and architectural innovations for improved humanitarian practice. proj.t: INTERIOR ECOLOGIES: Research on non-human environments
proj.d: The conference aims to bring together a series of transversal personalities who will address the subject of non-human architecture. From simple greenhouses to botanic facilities, data centres and automated interiors, never before in history has architecture produced so many interiors for the non-human, challenging disciplinary notions on tectonics, light and comfort, and entire regulatory frameworks. Once designed for and with the human, contemporary interiors have instead become exponentially complex materialisations where the politics of our present moment are played out. Elle a découpé, plié et assemblé la tôle à l'aide de tiges filetées, pour réaliser un porte-habits, mettant en valeur la transparence, la légèreté et la qualité structurelle de ce matériau. La tôle perforée révèle ici des qualités esthétiques, structurelles et formelles inattendues. Retransmis par les médias de masse, les événements importants, les phénomènes inquiétants sont soumis à des couches de lecture multiples avant d'être diffusés à l'opinion publique. Ces derniers ne sont-ils pas sujet à l'interprétation et à la manipulation des États, des pouvoirs, des médias? Sommes-nous pas la cible d'une désinformation systèmatique ? Quelle est la place et le sens des images dans notre société ? Le monde a enfin ouvert les yeux sur une réalité bien cachée et fascinante. Ce projet offre un regard critique sur le pouvoir manipulateur du designer, usant de stratégies de mise en scène, de narration, pour duper son auditoire.

proj.d: La lumière naturelle joue un rôle crucial dans la régulation de nos rythmes circadiens, qui dictent une variété de processus biologiques, des cycles veille/sommeil, notre niveau de vigilance et même la production d'hormones. proj.d: Les étudiant.e.x.s en Master d'architecture d'intérieur de la HEAD-Genève et Apropa Atelier vous invitent à une exposition sur la thématique du réemploi en architecture. Ensemble, ils-elles ont travaillé et questionné les différentes façons de re-penser la construction avec une approche moins impactante pour l'environnement. Identifier les bénéfices et obstacles du réemploi, réemployer des ressources existantes; penser des méthodes de construction qui favorisent la déconstruction plutôt que la démolition; rencontrer les acteurs du réemploi, sont les différents enjeux et recherches abordées. proj.d: Design Parade Toulon 5 e festival international d’architecture d’intérieur, 2021 du 25.06 au 31.10.2021 Un herbier est un spécimen qui devient sa propre image. À mi-chemin entre l’image, la maquette 1:1 et l’objet, l’herbier est multi-format. De la même façon, les intérieurs contemporains empruntent des directions multiples, de l’objet à l’image, du média à l’espace. Bien qu’ils existent dans des supports et des formats divers, les espaces deviennent physiques dans des instances et des itérations variées. proj.d: Avec la participation de Blanca Algarra Sánchez, Dany-Sarah Champion, Elizaveta Krikun, Filza Parmar, Karen Pisoni, Kishan Asensio, Lolita Gomez, Marion Vergne, Nina D’Elia Les diplômé.e.x.s 2021 en Master en Architecture d’intérieur exposent leurs travaux de fin d'étude. Cette exposition offre une opportunité unique au public de découvrir les travaux de diplômes, fruits de gros efforts après plusieurs années d’études. C’est également l’occasion pour les professionnelles et professionnels de venir à la rencontre de jeunes créatrices et créateurs et d’établir des contacts dans la perspective d’un premier emploi ou d’une première collaboration.
